title: SLO-driven proportional traffic shift with stream token preservation
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Objective: Implement a production-safe active-active traffic shifting protocol that is driven by per-route SLOs. The protocol must proportionally shift traffic away from a region or gateway when region-level signals approach SLO burn thresholds, while preserving in-flight streaming sessions and minimizing token replays and duplication. The feature combines: 1) SLO policy evaluation (latency/error SLOs) to compute a target egress distribution; 2) a gradual proportional drain ramp that respects open streaming connections by applying a lightweight 'token preservation' handshake and per-connection watermarking; 3) a circuit-breaker integration to rapidly shed new traffic if a region crosses critical failure thresholds; 4) load-shedding knobs (probabilistic reject, priority-based thin-client throttling) to protect stability.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Control plane exposes per-region shift percentage computed from SLO burn-rate within 95th percentile latency and error SLOs. 2) When a region is demoted, existing streaming sessions continue without replays; sessions are anchored to the original KV checkpoint and sped-forward in target region only if the checkpoint is successfully migrated. 3) New requests are routed according to the computed proportional distribution within ±5% of target within 30s of decision. 4) Circuit breaker trips immediately cut new connections to the failing region and surface telemetry. 5) No client-visible duplicate tokens observed in 99.99% of canary workflows.
design_notes: High-level flow: telemetry agents emit per-route SLO burn and latency histograms to the control plane. The controller runs a proportional allocation algorithm that outputs per-egress weights. The gateway applies a soft drain by decrementing existing accept-rate tokens for the region and tagging new outbound handshakes with a preservation header. For streaming sessions we maintain a small per-connection watermark (last safe token index) persisted to local KV and streamed to the control plane for checkpoint sync. On cross-region migration we attempt a fast checkpoint pull; fallback is to continue serving from origin region for that session until either the origin recovers or a cold-switch is agreed.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Preserving streams increases coordination and small KV read overhead; might slightly increase tail latency. - Aggressive proportional shifts reduce customer impact but risk oscillation; we mitigate with dampening and minimum hold windows. - Complete transparent migration for large sessions can be expensive; we prefer anchor-and-fallback by default. - Token preservation header leaks a bit of routing state; encrypt header in Private deployments to mitigate data exposure.
rollout_plan: 1) Small internal canary (10% traffic) routing non-critical routes with simulated failovers. 2) Extended canary with opt-in customers and high-observability hooks. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% of routes, run for two weeks. 4) Default-on for low-risk traffic, opt-out for regulated workloads. 5) Post-launch: tune dampening constants based on real-world burn patterns.
testing_plan: Unit tests for controller allocation logic, integration tests simulating SLO burns and region degradations, long-running canary with synthetic streaming sessions that include checkpoint/migration attempts, chaos test: introduce packet loss and delayed checkpoint reads, validate no token duplication. Add property test to ensure weight outputs are stable under noisy telemetry.
observability: Expose: per-region weight history, per-route canary error rates, stream-preservation success rate, checkpoint pull latency percentiles, circuit-breaker trip events with root cause tags. Add alerting: sustained >80% SLO burn for 5m, checkpoint-pull error rate >1% for 10m. Add dashboards in Console release runtime-1.24.
security_and_compliance: Encrypt preservation headers for Private deployments; flag security_review_required. Ensure audit logs capture migration attempts and decision timestamps. No customer data is intentionally replicated; only small watermarks and non-user PII metadata allowed in checkpointing path.
